qNotReady: This question is not ready yet.

qnum.ambiguous: “{unit}” can mean: {kinds} — choose a quantity so that the units of answers count.
qnum.converted: An answer in another unit of this quantity ({quantity}) is converted; a unit of another quantity is an error.

path.label: Path
path.use: A learning path as a map (like a course path): from the bottom — from the basics — upwards, with forks and places where paths meet (“2 of 3 paths”); each step is a hexagon: known (sunken, ✓), now (highlighted), ready to learn (raised, glowing), locked (pale, padlock), due for review (marker). From the base’s learning order (“Must know first”) — for a story (its entries; “now” is the place in the story), one unit (its parts), a view or the whole base. Click a step: “Learn” with what must be known before. Next to a story it stands alone — in the “Course / story” module it is already built in.
path.exEntry: <id or @name of a unit or empty>
path.entryHint: id or @name of the entry — its parts; empty: nothing
path.showsStrip: One line: how many steps are done and what is next — a “See” button.
path.showsTall: The whole map with step names; click a step: state and “Learn”.
path.showsBlock: A small map (collapsible) — follows where the learner is; click a step: state and “Learn”.

pathView.noStory: This story is not in the knowledge base.
pathView.noPresentation: This presentation cannot be opened here.
pathView.noSteps: There are no steps with questions here yet.

viewView.noCards: These entries produce no cards to learn.

viewPart.use: A saved view of a knowledge base (Learning → base → Entries → “Save as view”): chosen entries — also sermons and commentaries from the libraries the base uses — as a table, a tree with groups, a matrix (e.g. 20 mysteries × 12 periods; a cell opens its entries), a learning map, a progress map (tiles coloured by how well the visitor knows each entry — a click shows the text, questions and “Practise this”) or a landscape (in front of the visitor a ring of what they can learn now, further out mountains — the higher, the more steps are missing, behind them a valley of what they know; click: read, learn, revise, set a goal); a clicked entry opens below (commentary, the whole sermon), the path stays in the address. “Learn this” asks about the entries shown. Visible to whoever can read the base.
viewPart.modeHint: table, tree, matrix, map, quilt or landscape (also: tabela, drzewo, macierz, mapa, postepy, krajobraz) — empty: as saved
viewPart.switchHint: “yes” (or “tak”) — the visitor may change how it is shown and search in the view; empty or “no” — they see only what is chosen here
viewPart.missingView: Choose a view (saved in the base’s “Entries”).
viewPart.showsStrip: One line: name, how many entries, a “See” button.
viewPart.showsTall: The whole view: search, table, tree, matrix, map, progress map or landscape; a matrix cell, a tile and a clicked entry open below.
viewPart.showsBlock: The first entries of the view — the rest in full screen; progress map — up to 60 tiles; landscape — up to 24 fields.

question.label: Question
question.use: A question with an answer to check. In a presentation — a step of the flow: after a right and after a wrong answer it can lead to different places, and answers count in the browser or in Cogita. In a story with a knowledge base it can be a real question from the base ("question": its id or @name) — the answer then counts for what it is about, and together with revisions; an own question with "about" counts for the listed entries.
question.missValue: Choose whether the sentence is true.
question.missBack: Enter what is on the back.
question.answers: Right answers — each on its own line
question.exExplain: Baptism, confirmation, Eucharist, penance, anointing of the sick, holy orders, matrimony.
question.sPrompt: the question text (for a flashcard: the front)
question.sOptions: options, each on its own line (one, many)
question.sCorrect: numbers of the right options from 0, comma-separated, e.g. "1" or "0,2"
question.sAnswers: right answers, each on its own line (text, number); the back side (flash)
question.sValue: "tak" (yes) or "nie" (no) — whether the sentence is true (truefalse)
question.sUnit: unit of the right answers, e.g. "N·m" (number)
question.sQuantity: quantity (number) — e.g. "Torque", "Energy", "Mass", "Length"; then an answer in another unit of this quantity is converted, and a unit of another quantity is an error ("12 J" for a question about torque)
question.sTolerance: how far off an answer may be, in the question’s unit, e.g. "0,5" (number)
question.sQuestion: in a story with a knowledge base (a presentation with "story.base"): a real question from that base — its id or @name; then it shows itself (the fields above are not needed), and the answer lies on its card: it counts for what it is about (the question’s "about"), and together with revisions
question.sAbout: in a story with a knowledge base: for which entries of that base the answer to this (own) question counts — id or @name, each on its own line; knowledge of these entries grows with a right answer (landscape, path, conditions)
question.showsStrip: {form}: question and answer in one strip.
question.showsBlock: {form} — question, answer, rating and explanation; in a presentation then “Next” to wherever the result leads.
